name: Umbral-Mastaba
description: Sand owns this world, in colors from bone-white to burnt sienna, migrating with the seasons before a patient wind. Where the gusts strip it away, a tidally locked hemisphere emerge like the bones of the planet.

The air carries cold salt and iodine, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Glass-bladed grasses chime across the plains whenever the wind finds its voice.
The oldest impact basin predates the system's estimated age by a comfortable margin. The survey bureau has quietly stopped publishing the numbers.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
